etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English refreshen, refreschen, refrisschen, from Old French refrescher (“to refresh”) (modern French rafraîchir), equivalent to re- +‎ fresh.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Exodus 31:16–17:
quote.text: Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To become fresh again; to be revitalized.
(computing, transitive, intransitive) To reload (a document, especially a webpage) and show any new changes.

quote.text: She refreshed the page. She was still the high bidder. Good.

definitions.definition: (computing, transitive, intransitive) To cause (a web browser or similar software) to refresh its display.

quote.citation: 2007, Philip C Plumlee, Test Driven Ajax (on Rails):
quote.text: You can save your code, refresh your browser, and see a change instantly. This simple trick turns a lowly web browser into a development environment  […]

definitions.definition: To perform the periodic energizing required to maintain the contents of computer memory, the display luminance of a computer screen, etc.
(intransitive, colloquial, dated) To take refreshment; to eat or drink.

quote.text: We got within two miles of there, and stopped in the woods out of sight, where we refreshed with some brandy, and gave the two boys very large portions.

definitions.definition: The periodic energizing required to maintain the contents of computer memory, the display luminance of a computer screen, etc.
(computing) The update of a display (in a web browser or similar software) to show the latest version of the data.

quote.citation: 2013, Mark Phythian, Understanding the Intelligence Cycle, page 43:
quote.text: Experiences such as the Al Qaeda threat have provided a taste of how the landscape may have changed very fundamentally. Do these changes spell the end of the Cycle as a useful concept, or does it just need a refresh?
